title: Read the Filesystem Report
description: Save a df -h snapshot and extract the root filesystem's usage percentage into a report.
scenario: The capacity-review meeting starts in ten minutes and nobody has a current snapshot of the staging box's filesystems. Produce /home/intern/df-report.txt containing a full `df -h` output plus one machine-readable line: root-use=<used%> for the root filesystem, extracted from the df output itself.
symptoms: The capacity review has no current filesystem snapshot
The root filesystem's used-percentage must be machine-readable for the slide deck
The report file must contain the full df -h table as evidence
mission: Create /home/intern/df-report.txt containing the full df -h output plus a `root-use=<N>%` line with the root filesystem's used percentage.

hints.title: Human-readable units
hints.content: `df -h` prints sizes in K/M/G instead of 1K-blocks — the version humans (and slides) want.

hints.title: One filesystem, one line
hints.content: `df -h /` limits output to the root filesystem; `tail -1` drops the header; awk's $5 is the Use% column.

hints.title: Append, don't overwrite
hints.content: Save the table with `>` first, then append the root-use line with `>>` — the order matters.

acceptance_criteria.description: report contains the df header line
report contains a machine-readable root-use=<N>% line
report contains the root filesystem row (ending in /)
